name: frac_max
label: Burn extent (largest single fire-year)
notes: THE PROJECT HEADLINE. Bounded 0-1. Effect quoted at 100% burned.

name: frac_cum
label: Burn extent (cumulative across reburns)
notes: TRAP - exceeds 1 on reburns (max 4.47) so it is NOT a fraction; dose=1 does not mean 'fully burned'

name: frac_tot
label: Burn extent (in-window fires only)
notes: Sum of class 1-4 fractions for fires 2015+. Excludes pre-window burns that burn_frac_max can include.

name: binary
label: Burned yes/no
notes: SUPERSEDED - the diluted test. Median treated cell is only 29% burned. Provenance only.

name: mean_sev
label: Mean severity of burned area
notes: Area-weighted mean MTBS class 1-4. Ignores HOW MUCH burned - pair with an extent term.

name: max_sev
label: Worst severity class in the cell
notes: TRAP - SATURATES. 285 of 290 heavily burned cells return class 4. Useless as a gradient; this is why severity_effect.R section 4 finds nothing.

name: sev_weighted
label: Severity-weighted extent
notes: Frame column combining extent and severity in one number; scale is not a fraction

name: high_sev_only
label: Fraction burned at high severity
notes: Class 4 alone. Median is 1.7% of a cell so effects quoted at dose=1 are FAR outside the observed range.

name: mod_high
label: Fraction burned at moderate-to-high severity
notes: Classes 3+4. Less extrapolation than s4 alone.

name: two_dose_sev
label: Extent plus fraction at high severity
notes: Fixes Model A's power problem with TWO doses instead of four. Directly addresses 'severity' in the research question. OSFL high_sev t=+2.97 - the strongest signal found so far - but see high_sev_only note on extrapolation.

name: extent_x_meansev
label: Extent plus extent x mean severity
notes: severity_effect.R Model B - the one severity spec that worked (OSFL +0.0271 [+0.0006 +0.0535])

name: class_doses
label: One dose per MTBS severity class
notes: SUPERSEDED - Model A. Failed on POWER not collinearity (condition number 6.9 VIF<2); median class-4 dose 1.7%.

name: decay
label: Time-decayed burn
notes: Downweights older fires. Frame column; check its half-life in regrid before interpreting.

name: frac_recent
label: Extent burned in the last 3 years
notes: Fresh fire only. Tests whether the effect is driven by recent burn rather than old scars.

name: frac_old
label: Extent burned more than 10 years ago
notes: Old scars only. Should be near zero if the effect is about recent fire.

name: time_bands
label: Extent by time-since-fire band
notes: FIVE doses at once - a recovery curve without an event study. Power is thin per band. The y20p band was DROPPED 2026-07-31: in-window fires are 2015+ so no treated cell has a 20-year-old burn; the column is all-zero among treated cells and goes to exactly 0 under demeaning which makes the system singular.

name: sev_bands
label: Severity by time-since-fire band
notes: Severity within each time band. s20p DROPPED 2026-07-31 for the same reason as time_bands y20p - empty among treated cells and therefore singular.

name: n_epochs
label: Number of distinct fire years
notes: Reburn count. Max observed 11. Not a fraction.

name: reburn
label: Burned more than once
notes: Binary reburn flag. 99559 cell-times sit in cells with 2+ fire years.

name: nbr_frac
label: Neighbourhood burn extent
notes: TRAP - ambiguous when n_nbr=0 (9.8% of units get 0 meaning 'no neighbour visited' not 'no neighbour burned'). Filter on n_nbr>0 first.

name: cell_plus_nbr
label: Cell extent plus neighbourhood extent
notes: Separates in-cell burn from surrounding landscape burn. Same n_nbr trap.

name: fire_size
label: Log size of the causing fire
notes: From the MTBS perimeter table - NOT in the cell frame. Big fires differ from small ones in terrain access and post-fire management. NB commas cannot appear in a terms expression - the CSV would split - so use x+1 rather than pmax(x 1).

name: fire_season
label: Ignition day of year
notes: Late-season fires burn hotter and drier. Range roughly 1-365; consider centring before interpreting.

name: fire_month
label: Ignition month
notes: Coarser than fire_doy. Useful as a check that seasonality is not driving anything.

name: dnbr_calib
label: Per-fire dNBR high-severity threshold
notes: The dNBR value MTBS used to call class 4 for this fire. Varies by fire so class 4 is not comparable across fires - this quantifies that. TRAP - observed max is 9999 which is a MISSING-DATA SENTINEL not a threshold; only 1407 of 1956 CA fires have clean values. Filter high_t < 2000 before using or the sentinel dominates the regression.
